structure.note: Three classes: Class A has no votes, Class B one vote and Class C ten votes per share. The 10-K says co-founders Evan Spiegel and Robert Murphy 'control over 99% of the voting power of our outstanding capital stock as of December 31, 2025, and Mr. Spiegel alone can exercise voting control over a majority of our outstanding capital stock.' Item 12 gives Spiegel 53.1% and Murphy 46.4% of total voting power.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Document read on sec.gov: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0001564408-26-000013, filed February 5, 2026). Snap files no proxy statement (no DEF 14A in its EDGAR filings), and the 10-K itself carries the Item 12 ownership table, as of December 31, 2025. OWNERSHIP: Item 12 gives percentages per class (Spiegel 2.1% of Class A, 26.0% of Class B, 53.4% of Class C) and of total voting power (53.1%), not of all shares, so the economic share is given only as leader.derived (9.33%). His Class A count includes 3,027,844 shares, and his Class B count includes 5,862,410 shares, held in trust where he is trustee. His Class A holding fell from 39,063,540 at December 31, 2024 to 30,099,361. LARGEST HOLDERS left empty on purpose: the 5% holders are stated only as percentages of a class. Entities affiliated with Tencent hold 232,655,030 Class A (16.0% of Class A) and 10,344,970 Class B (45.9% of Class B); FMR LLC holds 96,806,403 Class A (6.6%, down from 14.6%); The Vanguard Group holds 95,317,701 Class A (6.5%); co-founder Robert Murphy holds 46.4% of voting power. None is a share of all shares, and recomputing is not allowed. BUYBACKS: $750.9 million of Class A repurchased for cash in 2025 (the $1,994.6 million of convertible-note repurchases are debt, not stock). PLAN: null. Snap has a 2017 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, but the 10-K says no shares of Class A common stock have been issued or offered under it. GEOGRAPHY: the 10-K says United States revenue was $3.4 billion in 2025.
